evidence: scripts/canary_bridge.py cmd_heartbeat_alert posts a comment on EVERY still-stale cycle (lines 239-244) with no daily gate
Run history (conclusion + timestamp) does not encode 'comment already posted today for this ticket'
findings.finding: The 'max one accumulation comment/day' element has no derivation source under the stated 'no new state store' constraint — workflow run history records conclusions/timestamps, not whether a comment was already posted today; with the */20 cron the accumulate path fires every 20 minutes.
findings.location: Approach — 'max one accumulation comment/day' + 'no new state store — the workflow's own run history is the durable state'
scenarios: Reconciler stale for a full day: without a daily cap the filer posts ~72 comments (every 20 min); the plan's stated once/day cap has no computable input
findings.suggested_fix: Derive the cap from the ticket itself: query the open tagged ticket's comments and post only if no accumulation comment carries a timestamp within the last 24h. This keeps 'no new state store' true (state lives on the ticket).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion that at least one filer path invokes the real `rebar create` end-to-end (or a contract-conformance test asserting the create args/exit codes against real rebar), not only mocked filer-logic unit tests.
evidence: Problem statement: 'silently break when create args/gates change (0e15/376d class: gate changes broke automated surfaces)'
Testing lists unit assertions on ticket/comment behavior but no live/e2e create; contract doc specifies 'exact rebar create args, exit codes' but no AC exercises them against the real boundary.
E5 proxy-validation: the critical path (actual create invocation) validated solely through offline substitutes can close green while the live path is broken.
findings.finding: The whole motivation is that gate/create-arg changes silently broke automated create surfaces (0e15/376d), yet testing exercises filer logic via unit tests only; there is no acceptance criterion that an actual well-formed `rebar create` fires end-to-end against real rebar. Mocked/unit filer tests can stay green while the real create args are malformed — exactly the failure mode being hardened against.
findings.location: Testing / Acceptance Criteria — 'Filer behavior covered by the unit tests above'
scenarios: A future gate change alters create's required args; unit tests mock create and stay green; the auto-filer fails to file in production exactly as in 0e15/376d.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a contract test that runs the documented create command against a real rebar instance and asserts exit code and the created ticket's fields, wired to the contract doc as the source of truth.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the per-check TAG derivation for the canary/heartbeat/binding-drift sites (e.g. a slug of the check name), matching the conflict-filer's explicit derivation.
evidence: 'dedup via a stable per-check TAG searched with has-tag (one open ticket per check)'
Only the conflict-filer tag ('derived from ... local id + jira key') has a stated derivation
findings.finding: The stable TAG format is defined only for the conflict filer (local id + jira key); the cycle sites (canary/heartbeat/binding-drift) get 'a stable per-check TAG' with no stated derivation rule, leaving the dedup key format to the executor.
findings.location: Approach: 'dedup via a stable per-check TAG'
scenarios: Two different checks in the same workflow must produce distinct, stable tags
findings.suggested_fix: Define the cycle-site tag as a stable slug of the check identifier (e.g. `autobug:<workflow>/<check>`).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State how dedup stays correct under concurrent/overlapping filer invocations (idempotent create keyed on the stable tag, a re-check after create, or a documented single-writer/serialization guarantee) rather than a bare search-then-create.
evidence: 'Dedup search runs FIRST: an existing open tagged ticket always takes the accumulate-comment path'
'the conflict filer ... gets dedup (stable tag derived from the conflict identity: local id + jira key)'
Search-then-create with no lock/CAS is a classic TOCTOU race; the plan defines the dedup lifecycle but not its concurrency safety under at-least-once/overlapping invocation.
findings.finding: The dedup mechanism is a check-then-act (has-tag search FIRST, then create if empty) with no atomicity guarantee; two concurrent filer runs (e.g. two concurrent reconciler applier passes filing the same local+jira conflict, or overlapping scheduled workflow runs) can both observe an empty has-tag search and both file, defeating dedup.
findings.location: Approach — 'Dedup search runs FIRST' / conflict filer dedup tag
scenarios: Two reconciler runs process the same unresolved (local, Jira) conflict concurrently; both has-tag searches return empty; two duplicate tickets are filed for one conflict.
Overlapping scheduled canary runs both cross the threshold and race the has-tag check, producing duplicate open tickets.
findings.suggested_fix: Rely on rebar create being idempotent for a given dedup tag (upsert-by-tag), or re-run the has-tag search immediately after create and close the loser, and state the single-writer assumption for each site in the audit table.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify what 'previous run conclusion' the threshold reads for heartbeat/binding-drift, given those filers keep the canary run green on red — either derive the previous red/green from the SAME per-check signal the current run uses (previous reconcile-bridge success age / previous bridge-fsck drift), or require the filer workflow to set its run conclusion to failure on red so run-history encodes the signal.
evidence: scripts/canary_bridge.py cmd_check_heartbeat derives 'stale' from querying reconcile-bridge.yml's last SUCCESS within an N-hour window (lines 94-158) — not from the canary's own run
cmd_heartbeat_alert files the alert and returns 0 (line 236-238, 269); cmd_binding_drift_alert files and returns 0 (line 384-386, 417) — the canary run concludes success even when it detected red
The ticket's parity note records the canary run concluding 'success' while classifying stale/fresh — the run conclusion is not the red/green signal
findings.finding: The consecutive-red threshold reads the canary workflow's own run conclusion, but the heartbeat and binding-drift filers keep the run GREEN on a detected red (both file via `return 0`), so the workflow's own conclusion does not encode the monitored signal's red/green — the threshold would over-suppress (never fire) or read a meaningless signal.
findings.location: Approach — 'CONSECUTIVE-RED STATE STORE ... queries the same workflow's previous completed run conclusion'
scenarios: Reconciler goes stale for 3 consecutive canary runs; each canary run still concludes success; `?status=completed` previous conclusion is 'success' every time; threshold never met; no ticket ever filed despite a genuine 2+ red streak
findings.suggested_fix: For heartbeat, compare the previous canary run's emitted staleness (or re-derive from reconcile-bridge run history at the previous canary timestamp); for binding-drift, persist/re-derive the previous bridge-fsck drift result. Do not rely on the canary workflow's own job conclusion, which is orthogonal to the monitored signal.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State explicitly how a 'red' run is recorded in run history (e.g., the filer step exits non-zero / the workflow fails on detected red) so `?status=completed` conclusion actually distinguishes previous-red from previous-green.
evidence: No plan text states the canary/heartbeat/binding-drift workflows set job conclusion=failure on a detected red
scripts/canary_bridge.py alert subcommands return 0 on the filing path (lines 269, 417)
findings.finding: The mechanism has an unstated precondition: 'previous completed run conclusion == red' only works if the filer workflow FAILS its own run when it detects red. The plan never establishes that the workflows fail-on-red, so `?status=completed` conclusions are effectively always 'success'.
findings.location: Approach — 'previous-also-red => threshold met; previous-green-or-absent => first red'
scenarios: A workflow that files but exits 0 always shows conclusion=success; 'previous-also-red' is never true; the mechanism degenerates to never filing

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Address concurrent-run dedup: either establish that filer runs cannot overlap (concurrency group) or make create idempotent under a racing create (e.g., re-search after a losing create, or rely on a create-time uniqueness on the tag).
evidence: scripts/canary_bridge.py _find_alert_ticket does a read (rebar list --has-tag) then the caller creates (lines 57-71, 213-235) with no atomicity between the search and the create
The e602 ticket's own parity note ran a workflow_dispatch canary concurrently with the scheduled cadence
findings.finding: The dedup is a check-then-act on the has-tag search with no concurrency guard; the plan does not address concurrent runs, yet scheduled + workflow_dispatch runs demonstrably coexist, so two runs can both observe 'no open ticket' and both create — a TOCTOU that produces the duplicate tickets the plan exists to prevent.
findings.location: Approach — 'Dedup search runs FIRST: an existing open tagged ticket always takes the accumulate-comment path'
scenarios: A scheduled run and a manual workflow_dispatch run fire within the same window; both has-tag searches return empty; both hit the create path -> two duplicate open tickets for one check
findings.suggested_fix: Add a workflow-level `concurrency:` group keyed to the check so filer runs serialize, and/or re-run the has-tag search immediately before create and abort-to-comment if a ticket now exists.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Justify the 'N>=2 consecutive reds' threshold against the windowed-ratio approach the cited flake bots (PyTorch/Flutter) actually use, or adopt a rolling-window failure ratio (query more than per_page=2) so alternating flakes are captured as the prior art intends; record the chosen threshold semantics and its divergence rationale in the audit table.
evidence: Plan: 'Per OSS practice (PyTorch DISABLED-test bot, Flutter flake bot, Sentry fingerprinting, Alertmanager for:)... file only after N>=2 consecutive reds'
Plan: 'previous-also-red => threshold met; previous-green-or-absent => first red, no ticket'
Verified prior art: PyTorch bot reports flakiness as a ratio over a window (e.g. 'flaky in 20 workflow(s) with 40 failures and 20 successes'), not consecutive reds
Verified prior art: Alertmanager notes only Prometheus's 'for:' (consecutive evaluations) can de-bounce flapping; a 2-sample consecutive check does not capture windowed flakiness
findings.finding: The plan cites the PyTorch DISABLED-test/flake bot and Flutter flake bot as prior art for the 'file only after N reds' idea, but then adopts an 'N>=2 CONSECUTIVE reds' rule (previous completed run also red, per_page=2), whereas those cited flake bots deliberately use a flakiness RATIO over a rolling window (failures/successes across many runs) precisely because flakes alternate rather than fail consecutively. The consecutive-2 mechanism silences the alternating red/green flake pattern the prior art targets, so the chosen design repackages the prior-art vocabulary without adopting its de-bouncing property.
findings.location: Approach / 'CONSECUTIVE-RED STATE STORE' paragraph; Acceptance Criteria line 'Consecutive-red threshold implemented via workflow run-history query'
scenarios: A check that fails on odd runs and passes on even runs (classic flake) never trips the consecutive-2 gate and is never filed, despite matching the flake-bot problem the plan cites
A genuinely-broken check that happens to have one intervening green (retried infra) resets to 'first red' and delays filing
findings.suggested_fix: In the Approach, add a sentence distinguishing the consecutive-red rule (aligned to Alertmanager 'for:', suited to a monotonic red/green cycle) from the windowed flakiness-ratio rule (PyTorch/Flutter, suited to intermittent flakes), and either (a) state that the canary/heartbeat/binding-drift surfaces are monotonic (not intermittently flaky) so consecutive-2 is the correct fit, or (b) widen the run-history query (per_page > 2) to compute a failure ratio over the last K runs.

findings.finding: The dedup/threshold pattern introduces cross-run shared state — a stable per-check TAG (one open ticket per check), a consecutive-red counter (N>=2 gate), a first-red timestamp, and per-day comment accounting — but the plan never says WHERE this state persists or how it is updated atomically. The core 'search has-tag; if none, file' step is a check-then-act sequence with no locking, so two concurrent or re-run workflow invocations can both observe 'no open ticket' and both file, defeating dedup (TOCTOU race).
findings.location: Approach: 'dedup via stable per-check TAG searched with has-tag (one open ticket per check); file only after N>=2 consecutive reds; max one accumulation comment/day'
findings.suggested_fix: Anchor dedup on the tracker's own has-tag query as the single source of truth (idempotent create keyed on TAG), and define counter/day-state persistence (e.g. in the ticket body or a labeled marker) so re-runs and concurrent runs converge on one ticket.

findings.finding: The plan claims to 'audit ALL existing auto-bug-creation sites and retrofit this same pattern' (USER-REQUIRED ADDITION a; AC#1), but the Scope enumerates only the canary/heartbeat/binding-drift filers (all in scripts/canary_bridge.py) and omits a fourth automated `rebar create bug` site: `_file_conflict_bug_ticket` in the reconciler applier, which files a bug per unresolved (local, Jira) conflict with no dedup tag, no has-tag search, no consecutive-red threshold, and no empty-detail abort.
findings.location: Scope section ('canary/heartbeat/binding-drift filer scripts or workflow logic'); Acceptance Criteria #1; USER-REQUIRED ADDITIONS (a)
findings.suggested_fix: Expand the Scope 'audit table of every auto-file site' to include the reconciler conflict filer, and state whether it gets the full pattern (has-tag dedup on a per-conflict TAG, threshold, templated body with abort-if-empty, detected_by stamp) or is deliberately out of scope with a documented reason.

findings.finding: The 'file only after N>=2 consecutive reds' threshold requires durable red/green state across canary cycles, but the plan names no store for it — and in this architecture the first-red marker has nowhere to live.
findings.location: Approach section: 'file only after N>=2 consecutive reds'
findings.suggested_fix: Specify deriving consecutive-red count from the reconcile-bridge run-history the canary already queries (or persist a small JSON marker on the tickets branch), and record the first-red timestamp there; only promote to an alert ticket on the second consecutive red.
